newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 29.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

* Walt Disney Co said it will explore options for divesting the newspaper and magazine publishing unit it acquired with ABC last year. The publishing unit could fetch about $2 billion, with potential buyers including Hearst Corp, KIII and Reed-Elsevier, the parent of Daily Variety.
* Time Warner's Warner Bros has pushed back the release date for "The Quest for Camelot," the studio's first full-length feature from its animation division, to the summer of 1998.
* Andrew Lloyd Webber's Really Useful Group downsized its British operations two weeks ago. The layoffs included at least two high-level executives and cut the group's London staff to about 60.
* Seagram Co Ltd's Universal Pictures has signed Michel Gondry to direct its screen adaptation of the TV series "Green Hornet."
* Fox's first Super Bowl telecast was its second-highest-rated week ever in homes and highest-ever in adults 18-49, with both the highest-rated night and single program in Fox history.
* EMI Latin is releasing the soundtrack to the Warner Bros film Selena, the story of the slain Tejano singer.
